stories.name: WPP, Adobe deepen global AI marketing partnership
stories.summary: On Feb. 24, 2026 WPP and Adobe deepened their global partnership to deliver a unified, AI-driven marketing solution by embedding Adobe Firefly Foundry into WPP’s agentic marketing platform, WPP Open. The collaboration combines Adobe’s generative AI, content platforms and data orchestration with WPP’s strategic, creative and media expertise to automate planning, creation, production and activation through agentic workflows that generate and adapt content while optimizing media spend. Firefly Foundry enables brands to train models on cleared IP so generated content is brand-safe and suitable for commercial use, and the integrated approach is designed to be privacy-conscious across the marketing lifecycle. The partners say the move tackles the industry’s pressure to produce more personalized content across more channels by streamlining fragmented tools and multistep processes into a single flow that frees human teams for higher-level creativity. WPP and Adobe also plan investments in training creative AI engineers to help clients adopt AI-led marketing processes and ensure human oversight remains central.
keyPoints: WPP Open is already in wide internal use across the group — more than 85,000 WPP employees use the platform.

WPP CTO Stephan Pretorius: “For years, we’ve watched brilliant creative ideas get stuck in production queues… With Adobe, we’re shattering the barriers between ideation and impact, building agentic content systems that handle the complexity so human creativity can soar.”

Adobe says Firefly Foundry enables development of generative AI models that are 'responsibly trained' on a customer's cleared IP and can be 'approved for commercial deployment', a phrasing the partners use to emphasise legal/brand safety for generated content.

stories.name: Telangana CM, Adobe CEO Discuss Investments, AI Impact
stories.summary: On Feb. 25, Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy met Adobe CEO Shantanu Narayen, a member of the Telangana Rising 2047 vision board, to discuss a roadmap for positioning the state as a global manufacturing hub and attracting major firms. The two discussed global manufacturing trends, green energy and the impact of artificial intelligence on the economy, emphasizing the need for skilling and reskilling to address job disruption. Reddy urged more cooperation from Narayen and called for new, aggressive plans by the state government to secure large international investments. The meeting aligns with Reddy’s broader push—outlined at the India AI Summit—for a national assessment of AI-driven job displacement and significant investment in workforce retraining.
keyPoints: The meeting was held at Chief Minister Revanth Reddy’s official residence in Jubilee Hills.
Shantanu Narayen’s visit was described as a courtesy call on the Chief Minister.
Details of the interaction were released through an official government release, which summarised the topics discussed and the need for a roadmap to attract investments.

stories.name: Adobe launches Firefly Quick Cut, auto-assembles rough edits
stories.summary: Adobe’s Firefly has a new Quick Cut feature that turns uploaded or AI-generated footage into a structured first cut from plain-language prompts, with optional scripts or shot lists to guide the assembly. The tool automatically selects takes, trims filler, inserts transitions (and can even generate brief transition shots from frames), and lets users set aspect ratio, pacing, duration, and optional B-roll while producing an editable timeline rather than a locked render. Firefly combines models from Adobe, Google, OpenAI, and Runway in a single app and Adobe is offering unlimited image and video generations up to 2K on select plans through March 16. Adobe frames Quick Cut as a way to eliminate grunt work and give creators a clear starting point while preserving creative control. Creators such as Brandon Baum and Sophia Kianni praise Firefly for speeding ideation and providing multiasset support for small businesses, podcasters, and marketers. Adobe positions Quick Cut as useful for both whole-project assembly edits and localized fixes, helping product reviewers, reporters, podcasters, and marketers iterate faster.
keyPoints: YouTuber Brandon Baum said he uses Firefly as a “thought starter,” adding: “I like to generate a few things, iterate on my ideas quickly, try, try, try, fail fast, and hopefully find the gold.”

Adobe product lead Mike Polner framed Quick Cut around speed and iteration: “When inspiration strikes, video creators need tools that keep pace with the speed of their minds... They need to fill their timeline quickly, so they can build on top of it and when necessary, tear it down and build anew.”

The March 16 promotion applies to specific Firefly plans (Firefly Pro, Firefly Premium, and 4,000‑, 7,000‑, and 50,000‑credit plans) and includes unlimited generations with several image models named by Adobe: Google Nano Banana Pro, GPT Image Generation, Runway Gen‑4 Image, as well as Adobe’s own Firefly image and video models.

stories.name: Major funds raise Adobe holdings
stories.summary: Multiple institutional investors raised stakes in Adobe Inc. according to recent Form 13F filings, with Vanguard Mega Cap Index Fund adding 8,837 shares to hold about 88,149 shares (~$28.2M) and Vanguard S&P 500 Growth Index Fund adding 2,710 shares to hold about 120,876 shares (~$38.7M). Eagle Global Advisors increased its position by 1,010 shares to 1,988 shares (about $695,780), while other firms including Leelyn Smith, Salomon & Ludwin and Allen Mooney & Barnes also reported meaningful increases (Allen Mooney & Barnes added 32,864 shares to hold 38,403 shares, per filings). The coverage highlights a broad institutional buying trend across both large index funds and smaller advisors. Reported market-market details show Adobe trading in the mid-$250s with a 52-week low near $251 and reported highs in the mid-$400s, a market capitalization around $106 billion and a price-to-earnings ratio near 15.5.
keyPoints: Allen Mooney & Barnes Investment Advisors LLC boosted its Adobe stake by 593.32%, purchasing 32,864 shares to bring its total to 38,403 shares valued at about $13,440,670.
Capital Group Growth ETF bought 31,632 shares of Adobe, raising its position to 246,352 shares worth approximately $78,864,670.
Sparkline Intangible Value ETF initiated a new position in Adobe, purchasing 1,142 shares valued at roughly $365,590.

stories.name: Adobe announces free creative tools for Indian students
stories.summary: Adobe announced a program giving students in accredited Indian higher-education institutions free access to flagship tools including Photoshop, Acrobat and Firefly, with access routed through participating colleges and institutions rather than direct public sign-up. The offering includes AI-first learning modules, structured curriculum and guided training, plus industry-recognized certifications through a partnership with NASSCOM FutureSkills Prime supported by MeitY. Adobe said the move is intended to boost AI skills and the country’s creator economy while aligning with the government’s digital-skill and 'Create in India' priorities. The initiative also plans to extend to thousands of schools and hundreds of colleges establishing Content Creator Labs to support practical learning. Company chair and CEO Shantanu Narayen framed the effort as empowering students with AI capabilities to help advance the nation’s development goals.
keyPoints: Adobe announced the programme at the AI Impact Summit 2026 in New Delhi.
Some reports describe the announcement as having been made in Chandigarh, indicating differing accounts of the event location in media coverage.
Adobe said this new offering extends its existing Digital Academy programme in India through the NASSCOM FutureSkills Prime partnership.

stories.name: Adobe Faces AI-Training Lawsuits, Analyst Downgrades
stories.summary: Adobe shares have plunged roughly 43% over the past year and now trade near $264 as investors reassess large software names and several firms (Goldman Sachs, UBS, Piper Sandler) have downgraded the stock, citing weaker near-term revenue and EPS versus peers. The company now faces renewed legal pressure from lawsuits alleging it used pirated books to train its AI models—new suits in February follow a December filing—which raises regulatory, reputational and financial risk for its AI roadmap. At the same time Adobe is pushing an enterprise AI strategy, announcing an AI-focused collaboration with Cognizant and promoting Firefly/GenStudio and Acrobat AI Assistant as monetization levers aimed at scaled content supply chains. Valuation views diverge sharply: a Simply Wall St. DCF implies a much higher intrinsic value (around $545 per share), while analysts cutting ratings highlight near-term execution risk and competition from AI-native rivals. The near-term investor debate centers on whether Adobe can translate its AI products into sustainable revenue and pricing power without legal setbacks eroding its creative and document franchises.
keyPoints: TV host Jim Cramer criticized Adobe’s positioning in the AI market, saying, "Well Adobe’s been cut in half. And I think Adobe, you can very quickly disable the 660 dollar Adobe [inaudible] that I have. I don’t need it anymore. I got the same thing going for 60 bucks. So that’s in trouble, that’s trouble."

A Bloomberg-reported lawsuit filed Feb. 9 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California alleges Adobe willfully used pirated books to train its AI models and cites infringement of hundreds of thousands of books.

Adobe’s published growth narrative projects $29.3 billion in revenue and $8.7 billion in earnings by 2028, implying roughly 9.0% annual revenue growth and about a $1.8 billion increase in earnings from $6.9 billion today — assumptions investors must accept for the bullish case.

stories.name: Canva Hits $4B ARR, AI Fuels Growth
stories.summary: Canva closed 2025 with about $4 billion in annual recurring revenue as monthly active users rose roughly 20% to ~265 million and paid subscribers exceeded 31 million, growth company leaders attribute largely to new AI features. The company doubled its B2B ARR to $500 million while remaining skewed to North America and pursuing lower-priced subscriptions in markets like Pakistan, Uruguay, Morocco and Jamaica to expand monetization. Management is repositioning Canva as an AI-first platform—a “design agency in your pocket”—anchored by tools such as Magic Write/Magic Design and an AI mini-app/website generator that has over 10 million monthly users. Deepening integrations with large language models and chatbots (including ChatGPT and Claude) produced millions of in-chat interactions (26M+ by October 2025) and rising double-digit LLM-driven referral traffic, creating a new low-cost discovery channel. The results validate Canva’s AI pivot and sharpen competition with legacy creative software vendors as LLMs emerge as a major distribution gateway.
keyPoints: Canva’s co-founder and COO Cliff Obrecht said the company is “inverting” its strategy—moving from a design platform with AI tools to an AI platform with design tools, calling Canva more like a “cursor for design.”

Canva is actively dedicating resources to appear in LLM-driven search results and is investing in SEO and content around user search intents because it sees ChatGPT and other LLMs as the new top-of-funnel for user acquisition.

Canva faces named competition from established players including Adobe and Freepik as well as Apple, which is pushing a bundled Creator Studio (apps like Final Cut Pro, Logic Pro, Pixelmator Pro, Motion, Compressor and MainStage) as a rival creative offering.

stories.name: 51 AVGC-XR startups expected at WAVES Corner
stories.summary: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw inaugurated the WAVES Creators Corner at the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi, highlighting the growing use of AI in creative content and noting India has onboarded more than 38,000 high-end GPUs (with plans to add more), subsidized access and large AI investment commitments tied to the summit. The WAVES Creators Corner, powered by the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting and facilitated by WaveX, brings 51 AVGC-XR and media-tech startups to the India AI Impact Expo to showcase AI-driven animation pipelines, real-time rendering, immersive XR, virtual production, gaming and content-monetization technologies. Demonstrations include a Zero-Touch Autonomous Newsroom that converts live feeds into multilingual breaking news, the Bhasha-Wall offering real-time lip-synced dubbing across multiple Indian languages alongside an AI sign-language avatar, and immersive exhibits such as Samvad Setu, The Director’s Chair, an AI podcast studio, conversational humanoid robots and voice cloning. The pavilion pairs these showcases with panels, masterclasses and industry collaborations — including Adobe’s Kathavatar and a masterclass by Shekhar Kapur — to discuss responsible AI, cultural authenticity and tools for preserving linguistic and cultural heritage. Overall, the showcase aims to position India as a leader in responsible creative AI by connecting startups, investors, policymakers and global stakeholders and shifting focus from foundational compute to India-specific design, R&D and productization.
keyPoints: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw singled out Kuku’s platform at the event, saying, “AI is being used very effectively in the world of creative content... you should definitely check out Kuku’s platform. It has immense potential.”

Under the IndiaAI Mission India has onboarded more than 38,000 high‑end GPUs and is expected to add another 20,000; these GPUs are available at about Rs 65 per hour — roughly one‑third of the global average cost.

Vaishnaw indicated AI‑related investments tied to the summit are likely to exceed USD 200 billion, with about USD 90 billion already committed, and that the government is in talks with several large companies on further AI infrastructure investments.

stories.name: Top fund warns few software firms survive AI
stories.summary: Nick Evans, manager of Polar Capital’s $12 billion global technology fund that outperformed 99% of peers over one year and 97% over five, warns that application software faces an “existential threat” from AI and has largely sold off his holdings in major software firms. He says rapidly improving AI tools — and companies building in‑house solutions — will replicate and undercut many application vendors, creating substantial valuation and free‑cash‑flow uncertainty. The market is already reacting: an ETF tracking U.S. software is down roughly 22% this year while semiconductor stocks have surged as AI boosts chip demand, with Nvidia holding a near‑10% position in his fund. Evans urges investors to be significantly underweight application software, warns that only a few firms will survive the reckoning, and notes that falling stock‑based compensation could force companies to use more cash, further straining finances.
keyPoints: Evans said Polar Capital has sold virtually all holdings in specific large software names — including SAP SE, ServiceNow, Adobe and HubSpot — adding, “We won’t go back to these companies.”
Beyond exiting most application software, the fund still holds a small position and some call options in Microsoft.
Semiconductors dominate the fund: seven of the top ten positions were semiconductor companies, with Nvidia making up nearly 10% of the portfolio.

stories.name: USISPF plans largest US delegation, India AI Summit
stories.summary: The US–India Strategic Partnership Forum (USISPF) will lead the largest-ever U.S. business delegation to the India AI Impact Summit, bringing more than 100 companies and over 120 senior leaders to New Delhi for the Feb. 16–20, 2026 event organized by India’s Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. USISPF announced a new Board AI Task Force, chaired by John Chambers, to push joint U.S.-India work on strengthening AI ecosystems, accelerating responsible, population-scale deployment, and advancing trusted, scalable governance frameworks. The delegation—reported to include CEOs such as Adobe’s Shantanu Narayen and FedEx’s Raj Subramaniam—reflects growing alignment between American companies and Indian policymakers on how AI should be built and governed. Organizers frame the summit (theme: “People, Planet, Progress”) as the first global AI summit of this scale in the Global South, with more than 35,000 registrants and a focus on moving AI from experimentation to real-world impact.
keyPoints: USISPF is participating as an "Official Partner" of the India AI Impact Summit, not just leading a delegation.

USISPF Chairman John Chambers characterized the US‑India AI relationship as “the defining strategic partnership of our time” and said the task force will leverage USISPF’s public‑private partnership experience to support AI development and deployment for “nearly two billion people across our countries.”
Delegation co-leaders such as Adobe’s Shantanu Narayen and FedEx’s Raj Subramaniam are expected to drive discussions on AI’s role in supply‑chain resilience and improving digital access.

stories.name: SaaS Market Reported $1T Repricing, IPO Freeze
stories.summary: The software sector has undergone a fast, severe repricing—dubbed the “SaaSpocalypse”—that has erased hundreds of billions to over $1 trillion in market value, driven by steep sell‑offs and large ETF declines. The rout accelerated in late January–early February 2026 after advanced agentic AI tools (notably Anthropic’s Claude Cowork and Opus 4.6) raised fears that agents can automate complex workflows and undermine traditional per‑seat SaaS revenue, prompting investors to rotate into AI infrastructure. The sell-off has frozen IPOs and M&A, produced dramatic single‑week plunges for major names, and begun to leak into other tech and high‑flyer stocks beyond pure software. At the same time, Deloitte says the “SaaS is dead” narrative is premature: incumbents are likely to evolve into full‑stack, agentic, outcome‑focused platforms, adopt hybrid pricing, and coexist with AI‑native specialists. For buyers and investors, the market is shifting toward capability‑ and outcome‑driven procurement and investing, with winners those who can reliably build, orchestrate, and govern agentic workflows—though disruption will vary across categories like dev tools, cybersecurity, productivity, and industry systems.
keyPoints: Market watchers point to Salesforce’s mid‑2024 collapse — a 20% one‑day drop after a rare revenue miss — as the early warning that the SaaS premium was vulnerable and helped kick off the shift in sentiment.
Between Jan. 30 and Feb. 4, 2026, nearly $300 billion in market value was erased from the application‑software layer specifically, a concentrated hit within the broader SaaS sell‑off.
The S&P 500 software & services index plunged about 26% from its late‑October 2025 peak, underscoring the severity of the sector’s repricing beyond isolated company moves.

stories.name: New Documents Show FBI Rebuilt Epstein Video
stories.summary: Newly released Justice Department and FBI records show the bureau authorized destruction in June 2024 of the master surveillance recording labeled 1B60 from Jeffrey Epstein’s Manhattan jail and later produced a reconstructed NiceVision screen-capture that left a 62-second gap around midnight on the night he died. The public July release therefore showed a timestamp jump from 11:58:58 p.m. to 12:00:00 a.m., a discrepancy that fueled widespread conspiracy theories. Attorney General Pam Bondi had blamed a nightly surveillance reset for the missing minute, but the documents indicate her explanation rested on an unverified technician theory and was undermined by the FBI’s disposal of the original files. The revelations prompted a scramble to recreate footage, increased congressional scrutiny, and criticism of the FBI’s evidence-handling and technical procedures rather than evidence of deliberate tampering.
keyPoints: Then–Deputy FBI Director Dan Bongino publicly promised the agency would release the original surveillance footage ‘so you don't think there are any shenanigans,’ a pledge that raised expectations before the reconstructed video was posted.
The FBI's master evidence item labeled 1B60 had been stored in a Bronx evidence facility before agents received authorization in June 2024 to destroy it.

An FBI digital-forensics specialist attempted to recreate the footage by screen-capturing the NiceVision system on May 21, 2025, a step that produced the low-quality reconstruction later released publicly.

stories.name: FDA recalls M&M's for undeclared allergens
stories.summary: The Food and Drug Administration classified a nationwide recall as Class II after Beacon Promotions Inc. repackaged and distributed more than 6,000 promotional 1.3‑oz bags of M&M’s across roughly 20 states without declaring milk, soy, and peanut allergens. The affected products were promotional/marketing repackages (branded with names such as Make Your Mark, Subaru, Adobe and others) rather than standard retail bags, and the original factory packaging does list those allergens. No illnesses have been reported, but consumers with milk, soy, or peanut allergies are advised to discard the repackaged promotional bags or return them for a refund. Affected states include California, New York, Pennsylvania, Texas and many others nationwide.
keyPoints: Beacon Promotions initiated a voluntary recall on January 26 for 5,788 units and expanded the recall on February 4 to include additional lot codes and products.
The recall covers two product codes: BB458BG (5,788 units across four lot codes) and BB471BG (541 units from a single lot); affected best-by dates range from December 2025 through September 2026.

Some recalled promotional bags carry lot code M1823200 with a best-by date of April 30, 2026, and branding on repackaged bags includes names such as 'xfinity' in addition to Make Your Mark, Subaru and Adobe.

stories.name: Adobe Ending Animate Sales March 1, 2026
stories.summary: Adobe announced it will discontinue Adobe Animate — the 2D animation tool that evolved from Macromedia Flash and has existed for more than 25 years — and will stop selling the app on March 1, 2026. Support and download access will continue through March 1, 2027 for non-enterprise customers and through March 1, 2029 for enterprise customers; Adobe urged users to export FLA/XFL and other assets before those dates. The company framed the move as a strategic pivot toward AI-driven creative tools and said new platforms better meet users’ needs. Adobe offered no dedicated, full-featured successor, instead pointing creators to other Creative Cloud apps such as After Effects (for keyframe work) and Adobe Express (for simpler motion). The announcement provoked widespread frustration among longtime users, creators and studios, many urging Adobe to consider open-sourcing Animate and warning the shutdown threatens workflows, jobs and archival access to past works.
keyPoints: Animate’s lineage dates back to 1996: it began as FutureSplash Animator, was acquired and rebranded as Macromedia Flash, became Adobe Flash Professional after Adobe’s 2005 purchase, and was renamed Adobe Animate in 2015.

Adobe posted an end-of-life FAQ on its support site and sent emails to customers announcing the shutdown; the FAQ includes Adobe’s wording that “Animate has been a product that has existed for over 25 years and has served its purpose well for creating, nurturing, and developing the animation ecosystem.”

Several creators and studios that still rely on Animate warned of real-world impacts — for example, the creators of the short-form series Chikn Nuggit and Salad Fingers creator David Firth said they still use Animate, and a Jackbox Games technical artist (Megacharlie) noted the app is used in many high‑budget TV, film and animation productions.

stories.name: Piper Sandler Downgrades Adobe, Lowers Target to $330
stories.summary: Piper Sandler downgraded Adobe from ‘Overweight’ to ‘Neutral’ and slashed its price target to $330 from $470, a nearly 30% cut. That move adds to a wave of recent analyst downgrades and target trims for Adobe by firms such as UBS, Oppenheimer, BMO and Jefferies, reflecting a more cautious consensus on the stock. Piper Sandler also downgraded other enterprise-software names and lowered multiple price targets across the sector, citing investor apathy and a thesis that AI-driven efficiencies could constrain headcount growth and revenue upside. The cluster of cuts has pressured Adobe shares lower as investors reassess growth and margin prospects for software companies.
keyPoints: The Piper Sandler analyst who issued the downgrade was Hannah Rudoff.
Piper Sandler downgraded three enterprise-software stocks — Adobe, Freshworks and Vertex — and also cut price targets on other large software names (including Salesforce).

Several other analysts recently adjusted their Adobe ratings/targets: Jefferies cut Adobe from 'Buy' to 'Hold' and lowered its target from $500 to $400 on Jan. 5, 2026 (a 20% cut); UBS kept a 'Neutral' view but trimmed its target from $375 to $340 on Jan. 26, 2026; Oppenheimer downgraded from 'Outperform' to 'Perform' on Jan. 13, 2026; BMO cut from 'Outperform' to 'Market Perform' on Jan. 9, 2026; and Citigroup maintained 'Neutral' but raised its target from $366 to $387 on Dec. 17, 2025.

stories.name: Figma integrates Weave AI, shares slump
stories.summary: Figma has acquired AI startup Weavy, rebranding it as Figma Weave and folding its AI tools into the core design platform to accelerate AI‑powered workflows. Management points to continued growth among large enterprise customers and recurring revenue—Figma has crossed roughly $1 billion in ARR and serves about 13 million monthly users, including most of the Fortune 500—suggesting healthy product adoption beyond designers. Despite those fundamentals, the stock has plunged to about $21.39, down roughly 40–43% over recent weeks and about 85% from its post‑IPO peak, erasing tens of billions in market value. Market responses are mixed: heavy options activity shows deep‑pocketed traders taking both bullish and bearish positions, while analysts' fair‑value estimates diverge widely (variously cited near $43–$66 or about $52), reflecting uncertainty about Figma’s outlook. Investors will be watching how quickly and deeply Figma Weave’s AI features are adopted, how enterprise usage and recurring revenue trends evolve, and whether competitors can match its AI capabilities before the valuation gap closes.
keyPoints: Benzinga flagged an unusual surge in options activity for FIG: 48 'extraordinary' trades in the period analyzed (29 puts totaling $2,692,098 and 19 calls totaling $1,201,238), with big players targeting strikes roughly between $12.50 and $55.00; the report also noted very high trading volume (about 18.3 million) and technicals suggesting the stock may be oversold.

Figma’s 2025 IPO was dramatic: the July 31, 2025 listing priced at $33, opened near $85 and closed the first day at $115.50, later touching $143 and briefly valuing the company at over $60 billion — a peak that has since shrunk to roughly $10.5 billion, erasing more than $50 billion in market value.

Beyond ARR and user counts, Figma’s underlying business showed strong operational performance: quarterly revenue was rising at close to a 40% year‑over‑year pace and the company was described as profitable on an operating basis.

stories.name: Barnsley named UK's first Tech Town
stories.summary: The UK government has named Barnsley the country’s first government-backed “Tech Town,” with Technology Secretary Liz Kendall and the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology committing support to trial AI across schools, businesses, NHS services and public infrastructure as a potential national blueprint. Over the next 18 months the programme will pilot AI tutoring in schools, offer free AI and digital training for residents via local colleges, expand the Seam Digital Campus to help small businesses adopt new tech, and test AI tools to speed hospital check-ins, triage and outpatient care. Major vendors including Microsoft, Cisco and Adobe have pledged support and senior executives will join Kendall in visiting the town to help boost local skills and infrastructure. Residents will be invited to “Tech Town Halls” to give feedback, and ministers say lessons from Barnsley will shape how AI is rolled out elsewhere in the UK. Local leaders hailed the investment as a major opportunity to revive a post‑industrial economy, though community figures and opposition councillors have warned of anxieties about whether AI will be a force for good even as the council already uses AI in services such as adult social care and road scanning.
keyPoints: The programme includes upgrades to Barnsley’s tech infrastructure such as installing Wi‑Fi in public buildings and strengthening cybersecurity for critical services.

The Seam Digital Campus already houses 33 tech companies and there are plans to expand it into an AI Campus centred on a new National Centre for Digital Technologies to help small firms scale and create local jobs.
In addition to Microsoft, Cisco and Adobe, some reporting names Google among the major tech firms that have agreed to support the Barnsley initiative.

stories.name: Adobe shares rebound near $280 after AI jitters
stories.summary: Adobe’s stock and options activity have shown heightened volatility as investors debate whether generative AI will erode subscription pricing or convert into higher-paid users, with shares recently rebounding near $280 even as implied volatility and bearish option interest rose following a Piper Sandler downgrade. The central market question is AI monetization—investors want tangible proof that Firefly, embedded AI assistants and other features are driving new paid seats rather than only increasing productivity for existing users. Bulls argue Adobe is leveraging AI to deepen its moat via Firefly Foundry for enterprise-safe models, broad partnerships (including Google and OpenAI) and integrations that expand its addressable market. At the same time, management is making strategic product shifts—most visibly the decision to discontinue Adobe Animate—framed as platform evolution rather than an explicit AI pivot. All attention now turns to the March 12, 2026 earnings report as the pivotal test of Adobe’s guidance, AI-driven recurring revenue targets and the status of the pending Semrush acquisition.
keyPoints: Options-market metrics show elevated bearish positioning and volatility: put/call ratio was about 1.18, implied volatility sat near 40.41 (up ~7 points), options volume ran roughly 66,000 contracts and traders were pricing an expected daily move of about $6.93.

On Feb. 2 Adobe updated Firefly subscriber benefits to include unlimited image and video generations and access to multiple AI models inside the Firefly app (not limited to Adobe’s proprietary models).

Adobe's full-year fiscal 2026 guidance calls for total revenue of $25.90 billion to $26.10 billion and targets Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) growth of more than 10%, accompanied by a new, more detailed reporting framework.

stories.name: Adobe Firefly offers unlimited image, video generations
stories.summary: Adobe announced that Firefly subscribers can now create unlimited image and video generations, removing previous monthly caps to let creators iterate freely. The change applies across Adobe’s Firefly models and supported third‑party engines including Google Nano Banana Pro, GPT Image Generation, and Runway Gen‑4. Unlimited generations are available on firefly.adobe.com, in Firefly Boards and the Firefly mobile apps, and extend to the video editor, sound and music generators and “Prompt to Edit,” with video output up to 2K and continued editing in Creative Cloud apps like Photoshop and Premiere. Adobe frames the move as helping creators stay “in the flow,” noting that 86% of creators now use generative AI daily and that average prompt length doubled in 2025. Adobe said subscribers must sign up for standalone Firefly plans by March 16 to get the lifted caps, and the offer does not apply to Creative Cloud subscriptions.
keyPoints: The unlimited‑generation offer applies to specific Firefly subscription tiers — including Firefly Pro, Premium and the named credit plans (4,000, 7,000 and 50,000 credit plans) — not just a single flat plan.

Adobe now distributes Firefly as a standalone platform beyond Creative Cloud: it’s available on the web and dedicated mobile apps for iOS and Android — and has even been released for Apple’s visionOS — after originally rolling Firefly out inside Creative Cloud apps.

Adobe and coverage emphasize that the unlimited generations are positioned to help small business owners and creative professionals experiment more freely — enabling rapid iteration for marketing, product design and branding work.
